properties.coordinate_basis: Placed on the tip of Otter Tail Point per the DNR Leech Lake shoreline polygon (site/data/lakes.geojson, DOW 11020300). The named road (E Otter Tail Rd NW) geocodes ~1 km inland of the shore; the post site itself is not surveyed.
properties.name: Otter Tail Point
properties.notes: Nute's second NWC post 'farther to the west as late as 1805' has no named location in the source and is NOT mapped as a separate point.
properties.source: Nute 1930 (Leech Lake (1), entries 54-55); Cass County Museum "Stimulated Exploration" marker (HMdb 235799); leechlake.org History of Leech Lake
properties.source_quote: The Northwest Company had at least two posts on this lake, one on Otter Tail Point about 1785 and the other farther to the west as late as 1805. (Nute 1930). The Northwest Company, a fur trading business that began in Montreal in the late 1700s, established trading posts in 1785 on Ottertail Point. (leechlake.org)

properties.coordinate_basis: Geographic center of Squaw Point, also known as Oak Point, as georeferenced by the NYBG Steere Herbarium (47.1693, -94.574; uncertainty 486 m). The marker does not attribute this post to one company, so company is recorded as NWC/AFC.
properties.name: Oak Point
properties.notes: Name changed from Squaw Point to Oak Point by the MN DNR Commissioner, Aug 6, 2007 (Cass County PWI 11-203).
properties.source: Cass County Museum "Stimulated Exploration" marker (HMdb 235799); NYBG Steere Herbarium specimen georeference for Squaw Point
properties.source_quote: Eventually the Northwest Fur Company and the American Fur Company formed and set up trading posts throughout the Leech Lake Area — one on Squaw Point, now known as Oak Point, another at Headquarters Bay, located on the east end of Leech Lake and Leech Lake Village, which later became the Village of Walker. (HMdb 235799)

properties.coordinate_basis: Placed at the center of Headquarters Bay, the far eastern bay of Leech Lake. Reference: Partridge Point in Headquarters Bay is at 47.104095, -94.277295 (Bell Atlas, +-800 m). The marker gives no shore side, so the point marks the bay, not a shore site; the post site itself is not surveyed.
properties.name: Headquarters Bay
properties.notes: The marker does not attribute this post to one company, so company is recorded as NWC/AFC.
properties.source: Cass County Museum "Stimulated Exploration" marker (HMdb 235799); Minnesota Biodiversity Atlas (Bell Museum) occurrence records in Headquarters Bay
properties.source_quote: Eventually the Northwest Fur Company and the American Fur Company formed and set up trading posts throughout the Leech Lake Area — one on Squaw Point, now known as Oak Point, another at Headquarters Bay, located on the east end of Leech Lake and Leech Lake Village, which later became the Village of Walker. (HMdb 235799)

properties.coordinate_basis: Pine Point Cir NW geocodes to 47.15341, -94.51731, ~96 m from the DNR Leech Lake shoreline. The post site itself is not surveyed.
properties.name: Pine Point
properties.notes: Nute also records a second AFC fort a mile north of Johnston's house and a contemporaneous post on the east shore (Schoolcraft map); neither has a named point location in the source and neither is mapped as a separate point.
properties.source_quote: The American Fur Company had a post on Pine Point in 1833. Near it was the house of William Johnston, the representative of a company working in opposition to the American Fur Company. A mile north of Johnston's post was another American Fur Company fort. One of Schoolcraft's maps shows a contemporaneous post on the east shore. (Nute 1930)

properties.coordinate_basis: Walker, MN city centroid (47.10166, -94.58407), ~248 m from the Leech Lake shoreline. The village/post site itself is not surveyed.
properties.name: Leech Lake Village / Walker
properties.notes: The marker does not attribute this post to one company, so company is recorded as NWC/AFC.
